title: SDK contributor onboarding playlist (notes)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, hands-on playlist for new or occasional contributors who want to make productive, low-friction SDK changes (samples, docs, small features, bugfixes). Focus is on fast feedback loops, safety (telemetry + CI), and leaving clear follow-up work for maintainers.

Audience:
- New hires rotating into eng-developer-experience
- External contributors/contractors doing small PRs
- Internal engineers shipping a one-off sample or patch

High-level goals (what 'success' looks like):
1) First PR merged within 24–72 hours of starting the playlist.
2) Contributor understands where to add telemetry and how to not regress token accounting.
3) PRs contain a runnable sample (tiny app / README snippet) and a test that verifies the shape of the SDK API.
4) Mentoring signal: contributor completed at least one pairing slot with a maintainer.

Playlist (micro-steps — follow in order):
1) Quick read (10–15m): repo README + CONTRIBUTING.md + API surface doc. Make a tiny note: what command starts a local mock server?
2) Local dev setup (30–60m):
   - run ./scripts/dev-setup (creates venv, installs dev deps, spins up rwd-mock)
   - confirm `make smoke` passes (embedding + text-generation smoke tests)
   - open sample/hello_redwood and run the sample end-to-end against rwd-mock
3) Pick a tiny first task (15–30m): docs typo, sample tweak, README clarification, or a one-line telemetry label fix
4) Create a branch and open WIP PR early—use the PR template (see checklist below). Tag @dx-mentor for a 30m pairing slot.
5) Fill in automated checks: unit test (or sample-level check), lint, and run token-usage guard locally (scripts/token-guard).
6) Add telemetry contract: minimal event id + fields (see Telemetry section). Add schema to telemetry/events.yaml and reference in PR description.
7) Iteration & merge: iterate with reviewer, squash/fixup as requested, and land. Leave a short follow-up TODO if broader changes are needed.

Mini-labs (runnable experiments you can finish in one sitting):
- Lab A: Add a new quickstart snippet for Python that uses the streaming API and asserts the first chunk. (files: samples/python/stream-hello.py, tests/test_stream_sample.py)
- Lab B: Add a note to the JS README about configuring region routing; add a tiny unit that parses a config JSON and validate with jest snapshot
- Lab C: Fix or add an integration test in samples/embeds that validates that embedding dims are stable across minor bumps (use deterministic seed in rwd-mock)

PR checklist (to paste into PR description):
- [ ] Short description of the change and motivation
- [ ] Which samples/docs are updated (paths)
- [ ] Tests added / smoke-tested locally (commands + output snippet)
- [ ] Telemetry events added / updated (event id(s) and schema ref)
- [ ] Performance note (if change affects runtime) or N/A
- [ ] Owners/Code-owners notified (add relevant reviewers)
- [ ] Manual validation steps (how a reviewer can run sample quickly)

Telemetry (practical rules):
- Minimum required for any runtime change: event id, light context (sdk_version, language, sample_name), and error bool. Keep payloads tiny.
- Add event schemas in telemetry/events.yaml and include schema version in PR. Example id: sdk.sample_run.v1
- For docs-only PRs, add no telemetry. For sample-run toggles, add a single usage ping guarded by opt-in env var (RWD_TELEMETRY=1)

Troubleshooting common friction:
- CI flakes on macOS wheels: run `pip wheel --no-binary :all: -w .wheels` and commit wheel cache pointer if allowed by maintainers
- Token-guard fails (token cost regression): run `scripts/token-compare old-output new-output` and attach the diff to PR. If cost increases > 15%, flag @perf-eng
- rwd-mock responds with 500 in smoke: ensure mock image is refreshed `docker pull ghcr.io/redwood/rwd-mock:latest`

Mentorship & pairing slots:
- Dx-mentors Slack channel manages a weekly pairing board (book 30m slot in the shared calendar)
- Recommended pattern: 10m context + 20m live pair to get the first green CI
- After 3 merged PRs, schedule a 1:1 retro with mentor to align on next steps

Acceptance criteria for a 'complete' contributor onboarding flow (for maintainers):
- PR has clear description and sample
- CI passed and smoke output included in PR comments
- Telemetry schema added when appropriate
- Reviewer leaves at least one constructive suggestion that was acted on
- Contributor signs off on follow-up TODOs (if any)

Housekeeping & longtail items (do not block first PR):
- Add contributor to CODEOWNERS if they will maintain a sample subdir
- Flag docs that should be converted from prose to short interactive snippets (follow-up ticket)
- Create a small 'first-PR' label and a triage rule to assign a maintainer within 48h

Unresolved questions / open decisions (please comment if you hit these):
- Should sample telemetry be automatically linked to a customer-product id for internal metrics? (pros/cons)
- Opt-in vs opt-out telemetry: current default is opt-out (RWD_TELEMETRY=0). Is this too conservative for internal E2E labs?
- How permissive are we about committing wheel caches for CI speed vs repo size? Need policy doc link.

Next actions (owners assigned inline):
- @Ethan Morales: add `./scripts/dev-setup` idempotency fixes (ETA 2026-02-19)
- @Priya Kapoor: draft the CODEOWNERS triage rule and label automation (ETA 2026-02-26)
- @Maya Chen: populate quick pairing slots in shared calendar and write short mentor guide (ETA 2026-02-16)

Notes to self (Maya):
- Keep playlist under 90 minutes total for a first-timer (aim 45–75min).
- Revisit token-guard thresholds after next SDK release (v1.4.0).
- Capture a 3min screencast of the 'first PR' flow and attach to CONTRIBUTING.md

Appendix: helpful commands
- ./scripts/dev-setup (bootstrap env + rwd-mock)
- make smoke (run quick generation + embed checks)
- scripts/token-guard old_ref new_ref --warn-threshold 10
- pytest -k smoke --maxfail=1
- bash ./scripts/record-telemetry-schema.sh <event_id>

End.
